To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ca2+ ATPase and calmodulin are associated with coated vesicles, and the association is not an artifact of the purification procedures.

the Ca2+-Mg(2+) ATPase activity is an intrinsic property of coated microvesicles (clathrin-coated vesicles) and that coated microvesicles can be purified by affinity chromatography on immunosorbent columns prepared by coupling antibodies against clathrin.
Ca2+ transport is a property of the coated vesicles and that the coated vesicle membranes are enriched in calmodulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to purify coated vesicles and the demonstration that these vesicles contain a Ca2+ + Mg2+ ATPase which seems to be an intrinsic membrane protein of the coated vesicles.
the purification and characterization of the coated microvesicular Ca2+ + Mg2+ ATPase.
the purification and characterization of coated vesicles from brain cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coated microvesicle fractions from ox forebrain are contaminated with plasma membranes but not with mitochondria.
Ca2+ ATPase is an integral part of coated microvesicles.
Ca2+ transport is an integral part of clathrin coated vesicle membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ transport by the coated vesicles may be a physiological function of coated vesicles in brain.

the Ca2+ + Mg2+ ATPase of coated microvesicles has a specific activity of about 9 mumol per h per mg protein and that the Na+ + K+ + Mg2 ATPase activity of the microvesicles is about 3.2 (+/- 1) mumol/h per protein.
the immunosorbants prepared with poly-specific coated microvesicle antibodies are useful for the isolation of coated microvesicle membranes with high Ca2+ + Mg2+ dependent ATP-ase activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+ ATPase is not a contamination of plasma membrane vesicles and mitochondrial membranes, but it is an intrinsic part of the coated microvesicular membrane.
Ca2+ -dependent ATPases in brain coated vesicles are not contaminants from other membranes but are integral to the coated vesicles themselves.
coated vesicles are a heterogeneous population of vesicles, some of which contain a Ca2+-Mg(2+)-ATPase.
